#178 implement.summary: The #178 fix is one commit, 78d432aa, on top of 8f7d98aa in /tmp/wt-178. It is not pushed. Before the fix, a delegated child's own strings reached the screen raw in two places. (1) The per-child status row, which the shipped TUI paints. The row goes through chrome._render_status and then prompt_toolkit's ANSI parser. That parser obeys SGR colour codes, and it writes anything between bytes 0x01 and 0x02 straight to the terminal. In the live TUI on base, a hostile current_tool sent an OSC 52 clipboard write to the terminal and turned the row red. (2) The progress card: format_card (panel._child_line and _queued_line), which ctx.on_partial sends to extensions and to json/rpc consumers. Fix: profile, state and current_tool on both surfaces now go through panel._flatten at PANEL_ROW_MAX_CHARS. That is the widget's own sanitiser and per-field bound, one function with no copy. current_tool is checked after flattening, so a tool name made only of control characters drops its term instead of leaving an empty separator. _flatten no longer uses its own restated C0/DEL/C1 table; it calls aelix_ai.utils.terminal_text.safe_for_terminal. The old table had drifted: on base, U+202E got into panel rows. So the widget, the batch status row and the result footer (tool._usage_field) now also remove BiDi overrides and isolates, ZWSP and BOM. Docs: ADR-0199 section (l) has a dated amendment (2026-10-08) saying 'byte for byte with P2' holds for clean input only and the card is sanitised otherwise. The ADR header line, the docs/decisions/README.md row, CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security, and a new section in docs/guides/agent-profiles.md (bundled copy synced) all carry it. Stale comments pointing at panel._CONTROL_KILL now point elsewhere. The work-bound test now counts what reaches the shared strip. citations.lock.json: 8 keys relocated with --fix, and I read each target. Sanitising happens at render time, not when stream.py reads the child's output. stream.py only sees current_tool and model; profile comes from the profile file and state from the runtime. SubagentProgress is a public contract another runtime may produce, and the bound is in terminal cells, which is a renderer concern. Probes, sabotage, live captures and the suite log are in /Users/handochan/dev/aelix-ai/.omc/probes/178-live/impl/.

owner_decisions: Identity is narrower than 'every string free of control and bidi characters'. A field is clean, and renders byte for byte as P2's, only if it has no steering character AND no leading, trailing or repeated whitespace AND is at most 78 cells wide. The other two clauses come from using the widget's own _flatten and width bound, as the task required. The alternative is a card-only strip that keeps whitespace and imposes no width bound; it would honour the literal wording but give up the 'same sanitiser and width bound' rule and the work bound.

The one-function rule widened the change beyond the two surfaces. The widget, the batch status row and the result footer now also delete BiDi overrides and isolates, ZWSP and BOM, because _flatten now uses terminal_text. ZWJ is kept.

The status row bounds profile and current_tool at 78 cells (the widget's per-field bound), not 16 (the aggregate's profile bound). An owner might want a tighter per-child bound on the shared height-1 row.

The amendment went into ADR-0199 section (l), which owns the 'byte for byte' rule, rather than ADR-0227 (the issue mentions the 0227 branch only as where the defect was found). No new ADR; 0256-0261 untouched.
Sanitising at render time rather than once when stream.py reads the child's output (reasons in the summary). Event-bus subscribers still receive raw child strings, as the contract documents.
follow_ups: [agents] consent._sanitize_field (spawn-consent dialog and the #196 disclosure status row) uses its own C0/DEL/C1 copy with no BiDi: a profile filename, source_path or cwd containing U+202E reorders what the human reads in the consent dialog. Move it onto aelix_ai.utils.terminal_text (contains_steering_chars for the refusal belt, safe_for_terminal for the strip), as #178 did for panel._flatten.

[tui] Restated C0/DEL/C1 tables without BiDi: tui/commands._CONTROL_KILL and _sanitize_child_field (the /agents result grid: child-authored model and provider), cli/agent_context._CONTROL_KILL and aelix_status/snapshot._CONTROL_KILL. Consolidate onto terminal_text so the next addition to the steering set reaches them; check overlap with #179 first.

[docs] extension-authoring.md does not say that the subagent_start / subagent_tool / subagent_end payload (SubagentProgress: profile, current_tool, model) and the agent tool's tool_execution_update partial text carry child-authored strings. Add one sentence telling subscribers that render them to sanitise (safe_for_terminal).

[agents] ADR-0199 section (l) still cites old panel.py line numbers in prose (panel.py:215-227, :252-273, :290-311); they are ungated and stale. Consider pinning or dropping them the next time section (l) is edited.

blocking.title: Docs promise byte identity, and say escape sequences are removed; neither matches the measured output
blocking.detail: (a) The ADR-0199 §(l) amendment and the panel._child_line docstring promise identity for any field with no steering character, no leading, trailing or repeated whitespace, and at most 78 cells. CHANGELOG says 'A name made of ordinary characters, in any script, is shown exactly as before' and the guide says 'as written'. A single non-ASCII space meets the ADR definition, but _flatten's split/join turns it into U+0020. Affected: NBSP, U+3000 ideographic space, U+2003, U+202F. No row pins this case. (b) CHANGELOG and docs/guides/agent-profiles.md (and its bundled copy) say 'control characters, escape sequences and BiDi overrides are removed'. Only the ESC byte goes; the rest of the sequence stays on screen as text. (c) The guide's '(78 columns for a profile or tool name, 40 for the model)' is stated for 'those rows', which includes the batch row. That row cuts the profile at 16 cells and the panel header cuts the model at 32. Fix is wording only: name the whitespace normalisation in 'clean', say the sequences are defanged, scope the widths. Optionally add an NBSP row.
